name: Rennellese Sign Language
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Sign language (Kuschel 1973 monograph is on sign creation, not word stress); no stress description exists

sources.citation: Bickford, Albert / ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2016. Change Request 2016-002: retire [rsi] Rennellese Sign Language (adopted 2017-01-31). SIL International. 5 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Rationale (p. 2): the system 'would clearly be considered a home sign system today', used by one deaf person and his hearing associates; Kuschel 'was unable to ever document any grammatical structure'. Cites Kuschel 1974 with the bellona.dk PDF URL.

sources.citation: Kuschel, Rolf. 1974. A Lexicon of Signs from a Polynesian Outliner Island: A Description of 217 Signs as Developed and Used by Kagobai, the Only Deaf-Mute of Rennell Island. Psykologisk Skriftserie 8. Kobenhavn: Psykologisk Laboratorium, Kobenhavns Universitet. 187 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on word stress or accent (signed home-sign lexicon, 217 entries). p. 19: only isolated signs could be recorded, description of syntax/grammar deferred. p. 32: reduplication of a movement is frequent but never changes meaning; intensity of execution expresses emphasis. p. 29: facial expression functions as a 'para-sign-language'.
Nothing. Classified 'Artificial Language', extinct, ISO code retired 2017-01-31 under CR 2016-002; no descriptive references listed beyond Kuschel 1973/1974 and the ISO request.

Nothing on grammar, phonology or prosody. States it is an extinct home sign developed ca. 1915 by Kagobai, Kuschel the only source; lists Kuschel 1987 'Renellese' in the Gallaudet Encyclopedia of Deaf People and Deafness vol. 3, pp. 105-106 as further reading.

sources.citation: Kuschel, Rolf. 1987. Renellese. In John V. Van Cleve (ed.), Gallaudet Encyclopedia of Deaf People and Deafness, vol. 3, 105-106. New York: McGraw-Hill.

sources.note: Two-page encyclopedia summary by the same author; could only restate Kuschel 1973/1974, which contain no stress description.

sources.citation: Kuschel, Rolf. 1973. The Silent Inventor: The Creation of a Sign Language by the Only Deaf-Mute on a Polynesian Island. Sign Language Studies 3: 1-27.

sources.note: The only other primary description of Kagobai's system; a psychological account of sign creation rather than a structural one, so very unlikely to contain a stress or prosody statement, but it is the one unopened primary item.
